findings.claim: `tprod_nonneg` takes `[L.NeBot]`, but the statement holds without it. When `¬ L.NeBot`, `tprod_bot` rewrites `∏'[L]` to `∏ᶠ`, and a finprod of nonnegative factors is nonnegative (it is either 1 or a finite product). Its neighbours in this file are written to avoid this hypothesis. `one_le_tprod` (whose additive form is `tsum_nonneg`), `tprod_le_one` and `tprod_le_of_prod_le'` each handle the `¬ L.NeBot` case explicitly. Only the `HasProd`-level lemmas (`HasProd.one_le`, `HasProd.le_one`, and the new `HasProd.nonneg`) keep `[L.NeBot]`, and they need it because `HasProd f a ⊥` holds for every `a`. Keeping the extra hypothesis makes `tprod_nonneg` unusable for a caller with a generic `L`. An example is a `tprod` analogue of the `evalTsum` positivity extension at the end of this file: `evalTsum` applies `@tsum_nonneg … $L …` to an arbitrary `$L` and has no `NeBot` instance to supply. Also, the `Multipliable` branch repeats the body of `HasProd.nonneg` (`ge_of_tendsto' … prod_nonneg …`) instead of calling it.
findings.requested_change:
Remove `[L.NeBot]` from `tprod_nonneg` and split on `L.NeBot` the same way `tprod_le_one` does, reusing the new `HasProd` lemma. For example:
```
theorem tprod_nonneg [CommMonoidWithZero α] [TopologicalSpace α] [Preorder α] [ZeroLEOneClass α]
    [PosMulMono α] [ClosedIciTopology α] {f : ι → α} (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) :
    0 ≤ ∏'[L] x, f x := by
  by_cases h : Multipliable f L
  · by_cases hL : L.NeBot
    · exact h.hasProd.nonneg hf
    · simp only [tprod_bot hL]
      exact finprod_induction (0 ≤ ·) zero_le_one (fun _ _ ↦ mul_nonneg) hf
  · simp [tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable h]
```
Keep `[L.NeBot]` on `HasProd.nonneg`, where it is needed.

review_notes: I checked whether the PR should also add another operation. Callers that already know the product converges to a given value (`HasProd f a L`) can use the new `HasProd.nonneg`, which follows the non-strict `HasProd.one_le`/`one_le_tprod` pair. A `Multipliable.tprod_nonneg` would add nothing because `tprod_nonneg` needs no multipliability. A strict analogue of `Multipliable.one_lt_tprod`/`hasProd_lt` (`HasProd.pos`/`tprod_pos` from `0 < f i`) would be false: the factors 1/2 multiply to 0. That analogy fails, so I did not request an extra lemma. A positivity extension for `tprod` is out of scope. The one finding comes from the file itself: `one_le_tprod`, `tprod_le_one`, `tprod_le_of_prod_le'` and the `evalTsum` call of `tsum_nonneg` with an arbitrary `L` show the convention of not requiring `L.NeBot` for `tprod` bounds, while `HasProd.*` keeps it because it is needed there. I did not compile the suggested proof. It follows the `finprod_induction` pattern in `tprod_le_one`, and `mul_nonneg`/`zero_le_one` only need the `PosMulMono`/`ZeroLEOneClass` instances the lemma already has. Separate style points (lemma vs theorem, the binder name, the `simp` in the non-multipliable branch) don't need changes.
